title: Over 1,000 Hongkongers to ride Baidu’s robotaxis in city-first public trial
key_facts: Baidu's Apollo Go launches its first public trial ride event in Hong Kong, running 21 Oct to 3 Nov 2026 in Tung Chung.
The 14-day event offers free rides and expects more than 1,000 people.
Each ride is about 15 minutes and about 5.1 km; each vehicle carries two passengers and the front passenger seat is not available.
Tickets are distributed by district offices from Friday 16 Oct; only people with physical tickets can ride.
Apollo Go was the first company in Hong Kong to get an autonomous-vehicle pilot licence; its cars have covered more than 280,000 km in the city.
quote_evidence: The 14-day event will run from Oct. 21 to Nov. 3 in Tung Chung, offering free rides and expecting to accommodate more than 1,000 people.
Tickets for the public trial will be distributed by district offices starting Friday (Oct. 16).
Apollo Go, a self-driving mobility service under Baidu, was the first company in HK to obtain a pilot licence for autonomous vehicles.
why_it_matters_hint: First time ordinary Hong Kong residents can ride a robotaxi, in a short supervised trial.
event_date: Announced 15 Oct 2026; trial 21 Oct to 3 Nov 2026
